body.statement:
For a fixed \(K\), suppose there is a single number \(\kappa_K>0\), chosen before \(a\), such that for every \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\) the ambient class \(\mathcal P_K(a)\) contains a law whose \((X,W)\)-marginal has mass function \(q_a\), marginals \(q_{a,X},q_{a,W}\), and conditional-expectation operator \(A_a\) satisfying
\[
\begin{gathered}
q_a(x,w)\ge \kappa_K\quad\text{for every }(x,w)\in\mathcal X_K\times\mathcal W_K,\\
q_{a,X}(x)-\frac{\eta}{K}\ge\kappa_K,
\qquad \frac{1}{\eta K}-q_{a,X}(x)\ge\kappa_K
\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X_K,\\
q_{a,W}(w)-\frac{\eta}{K}\ge\kappa_K,
\qquad \frac{1}{\eta K}-q_{a,W}(w)\ge\kappa_K
\quad\text{for every }w\in\mathcal W_K,
\end{gathered}
\]
and, for every \(g\in\ell^2_{K,W}\) with \(E_{q_a}\{g(W)\}=0\),
\[
(c_{\rm link}+\kappa_K)\|L^{-a}g\|_{\ell^2_{K,W}}
\le \|A_ag\|_{L^2(q_{a,X})}
\le (C_{\rm link}-\kappa_K)\|L^{-a}g\|_{\ell^2_{K,W}}.
\]
Then there are laws \(P_{0,a},P_{t,a}\in\mathcal P_K(a)\), having this same \((X,W)\) design and hence preserving every displayed slack, such that \(P_{0,a}\) is strictly positive, \(d(P_{0,a})=0\), and \(d(P_{t,a})=t\) for \(0<t\le\eta/2\), while
\[
D_{\rm KL}(P_{t,a}\|P_{0,a})\le\frac{t^2}{\eta(1-\eta)}
\]
and
\[
\chi^2(P_{t,a}^{\otimes n},P_{0,a}^{\otimes n})
\le \exp\!\left\{\frac{nt^2}{\eta(1-\eta)}\right\}-1.
\]
Consequently, for every \(\epsilon_{\rm tot}\in(0,1)\), there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(a\) and \(n\), such that
\[
\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\ge c n^{-1/2}.
\]
Together with \(\mathrm{thm:fixed\mbox{-}k\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\), this gives \(\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\asymp n^{-1/2}\) uniformly in \(a\) for every fixed \(K\) satisfying the displayed common-design premise.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(K\) and let \(\kappa_K\) be the single constant in the premise.  Fix an arbitrary \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\), and choose the asserted ambient law only to obtain its \((X,W)\) mass function \(q_a\), marginals, and operator \(A_a\).  All expectations in the first part of the proof are with respect to this design.

The bridge class is nonempty.  Indeed, the constant function \(h_{1/2}(w)=1/2\) has DCT coefficients \(\theta_1=1/2\) and \(\theta_j=0\) for \(j\ge2\), so
\[
\sum_{j=1}^K j^{2\beta}\theta_j^2=\frac14<R^2
\]
because \(R>1/2\), and \(\eta<h_{1/2}(w)<1-\eta\) because \(0<\eta<1/2\).  Thus \(h_{1/2}\in\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\).  The coefficient set defining \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\) is closed and bounded in \(\mathbb R^K\), hence compact.  The map
\[
h\longmapsto E_{q_a}\{h(W)\}
\]
is linear and continuous on this finite-dimensional set.  It therefore has a maximizer \(h_a^*\).  Define
\[
M_a=E_{q_a}\{h_a^*(W)\},
\qquad p_{0,a}(x)=(A_ah_a^*)(x).
\]
Since \(h_a^*(w)\in[\eta,1-\eta]\) for every \(w\), conditional averaging gives
\[
\eta\le p_{0,a}(x)\le1-\eta
\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X_K. \tag{1}
\]

Retain the design \(q_a\) and define two full observed-data laws by
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{0,a}(X=x,W=w,Y=y)
&=q_a(x,w)p_{0,a}(x)^y\{1-p_{0,a}(x)\}^{1-y},\\
P_{t,a}(X=x,W=w,Y=y)
&=q_a(x,w)\{p_{0,a}(x)+t\}^y
  \{1-p_{0,a}(x)-t\}^{1-y},
\end{aligned} \tag{2}
\]
where \(0<t\le\eta/2\).  By (1),
\[
\eta\le p_{0,a}(x)+t\le1-\frac\eta2. \tag{3}
\]
The cell bound \(q_a(x,w)\ge\kappa_K\), (1), and (3) imply
\[
P_{0,a}(x,w,y)\ge\kappa_K\eta,
\qquad P_{t,a}(x,w,y)\ge\frac{\kappa_K\eta}{2}, \tag{4}
\]
so both probability tables are strictly positive.  More importantly, (2) changes only the Bernoulli outcome kernel.  The \((X,W)\) law, its marginals, and \(A_a\) are unchanged.  Every member property in \(\mathrm{def:model\mbox{-}class}\) therefore follows directly from the displayed premise, with the same \(\kappa_K\) slacks.  Hence
\[
P_{0,a},P_{t,a}\in\mathcal P_K(a). \tag{5}
\]
This conclusion concerns the ambient class itself; it invokes no preservation property of any auxiliary subclass.

Under (2), the two conditional-mean functions are
\[
b_{0,a}=A_ah_a^*,
\qquad b_{t,a}=A_ah_a^*+t\mathbf 1. \tag{6}
\]
The first equality and \(h_a^*\in\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\) give \(d(P_{0,a})=0\) by \(\mathrm{def:observable\mbox{-}defect}\).  For arbitrary \(h\in\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\), Cauchy--Schwarz in \(L^2(q_{a,X})\), the identity \(\|\mathbf1\|_{L^2(q_{a,X})}=1\), and iterated expectation yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|b_{t,a}-A_ah\|_{L^2(q_{a,X})}
&\ge \left|E_{q_a}\{b_{t,a}(X)-(A_ah)(X)\}\right|\\
&=M_a+t-E_{q_a}\{h(W)\}\\
&\ge t, 
\end{aligned} \tag{7}
\]
where the last inequality is the maximizing property of \(h_a^*\).  Taking \(h=h_a^*\) in (6) makes the residual equal to \(t\mathbf1\), whose norm is \(t\).  Thus
\[
d(P_{t,a})=t. \tag{8}
\]
This also gives the advertised transverse geometry.  The functional \(z\mapsto\langle z,\mathbf1\rangle_{L^2(q_{a,X})}\) exposes the maximizing face
\[
\left\{A_ah:h\in\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta),\ E_{q_a}h(W)=M_a\right\}
\]
of the image, (6) places \(b_{0,a}\) on that face, and \(b_{t,a}=b_{0,a}+t\mathbf1\) moves in its outward supporting-normal direction.  The maximizer cannot be an interior point of \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\): the class has nonempty interior by the strict inequalities verified for \(h_{1/2}\), and an interior maximizer could be perturbed by a sufficiently small positive multiple of \(\mathbf1\), increasing its expectation while remaining feasible.

Because of (4), \(P_{t,a}\ll P_{0,a}\).  Direct summation over \(Y\in\{0,1\}\), conditional on \(X\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\chi^2(P_{t,a},P_{0,a})
&=E_{q_{a,X}}\!\left[
  \frac{t^2}{p_{0,a}(X)}+
  \frac{t^2}{1-p_{0,a}(X)}\right]\\
&=E_{q_{a,X}}\!\left[
  \frac{t^2}{p_{0,a}(X)\{1-p_{0,a}(X)\}}\right]\\
&\le\frac{t^2}{\eta(1-\eta)},
\end{aligned} \tag{9}
\]
where the last step uses (1).  If \(Z=dP_{t,a}/dP_{0,a}\), then \(\log Z\le Z-1\) and change of measure imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_{\rm KL}(P_{t,a}\|P_{0,a})
&=E_{P_{t,a}}\log Z\\
&\le E_{P_{t,a}}(Z-1)
=E_{P_{0,a}}\{Z(Z-1)\}\\
&=E_{P_{0,a}}(Z-1)^2
=\chi^2(P_{t,a},P_{0,a})\\
&\le\frac{t^2}{\eta(1-\eta)}. 
\end{aligned} \tag{10}
\]
The penultimate equality uses \(E_{P_{0,a}}Z=1\).

Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}sampling}\), product likelihood ratios factor.  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
1+\chi^2(P_{t,a}^{\otimes n},P_{0,a}^{\otimes n})
&=\{1+\chi^2(P_{t,a},P_{0,a})\}^n\\
&\le\exp\!\left\{n\chi^2(P_{t,a},P_{0,a})\right\}\\
&\le\exp\!\left\{\frac{nt^2}{\eta(1-\eta)}\right\},
\end{aligned} \tag{11}
\]
which is the claimed product bound after subtracting one.

It remains to translate (11) into a testing converse.  For probability laws \(Q\ll P\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\|Q-P\|_{\rm TV}
=\frac12E_P\left|\frac{dQ}{dP}-1\right|
\le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(Q,P)}. \tag{12}
\]
For any possibly randomized test \(0\le\phi\le1\), the definition of total variation gives
\[
E_P\phi+E_Q(1-\phi)
=1-\{E_Q\phi-E_P\phi\}
\ge1-\|Q-P\|_{\rm TV}. \tag{13}
\]
Set
\[
c=\min\!\left\{\frac\eta2,
\sqrt{\eta(1-\eta)\log\!\left(1+(1-\epsilon_{\rm tot})^2\right)}\right\}>0,
\qquad t=\frac{c}{\sqrt n}. \tag{14}
\]
Since \(n\ge1\), (14) ensures \(0<t\le\eta/2\).  Equations (11)--(14), with \(P=P_{0,a}^{\otimes n}\) and \(Q=P_{t,a}^{\otimes n}\), yield
\[
E_{P_{0,a}^{\otimes n}}\phi+E_{P_{t,a}^{\otimes n}}(1-\phi)
\ge1-\frac{1-\epsilon_{\rm tot}}2
=\frac{1+\epsilon_{\rm tot}}2
>\epsilon_{\rm tot}. \tag{15}
\]
By (5) and (8), the first law in (15) is in the composite null and the second is in the alternative with defect \(t\).  Thus every test has total error exceeding \(\epsilon_{\rm tot}\) at separation \(t\).  Monotonicity of the alternative sets in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\mbox{-}radius}\) proves
\[
\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\ge \frac{c}{\sqrt n}. \tag{16}
\]
The constant in (14) is independent of \(a\) and \(n\).  Since \(a\) was arbitrary and the same \(\kappa_K\) was assumed before choosing \(a\), (16) is uniform over \([a_L,a_U]\).  The premise also makes \(\mathcal P_K(a)\) nonempty, so combining (16) with \(\mathrm{thm:fixed\mbox{-}k\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\) gives the asserted fixed-support equivalence.
body.justification: The transverse construction gives an exact-defect two-point experiment and matches the attainable root-\(n\) scale for every fixed support satisfying the explicit common-design premise.
body.gap: The converse is conditional on the ambient classes admitting \( (X,W) \) designs whose cell, marginal, and two link slacks share one positive lower bound over \(a\); it makes no claim about preserving an auxiliary regular subclass.
body.consumer: Fixed-table implementations obtain a sharp total-error benchmark, while growing-table arguments can reuse the exposed-face construction only after verifying a suitably uniform design premise.
